What you'll learn

Six skills that change how you write grants

By the end of the course, you'll have frameworks, templates, and practice behind every major part of a competitive proposal.

01

Evaluate funder fit

Know when to apply and when to pass. Decode RFPs and foundation priorities the way a program officer reads them — saving weeks on proposals that were never going to score.

02

Shape a project narrative

Turn your program into a compelling story. Build a clear theory of change and need statement that speaks to funder priorities without losing your organization's voice.

03

Write strong outcomes

Learn to write SMART outcomes and evaluation plans that reviewers trust — even without a research department or external evaluator on staff.

04

Build a budget

Construct line-item budgets with clear narratives, handle indirect costs, and avoid the common budget mistakes that raise red flags for program officers reviewing your application.

05

Avoid proposal mistakes

Learn the most common reasons good programs get rejected — vague logic models, mismatched budgets, weak executive summaries — and how to catch them before submission.

06

Build reusable materials

Leave with a grant calendar, organization boilerplate, and reusable narrative sections so every future proposal starts from a stronger foundation, not a blank page.

How the course works

Structured learning that fits your workweek

Designed for development staff who are already stretched thin. Each week builds on the last — live sessions give you structure, recordings give you flexibility.

Live Tuesdays, 1pm ET

90-minute sessions each Tuesday. Elena leads with instruction and real examples, then opens up for Q&A and group work. No performance anxiety — participation is optional.

Recordings available

Every session is recorded and posted within 24 hours. Catch up on your schedule. Rewatch the budget section four times if you need to — no judgment.

Weekly worksheets

Practical exercises you can apply to a real grant you're working on. By the end of week six, you'll have actual sections drafted — not just notes from a class.

Real credentials

Elena spent eight years as a foundation program officer reviewing hundreds of proposals. The examples in this course are drawn from what she actually saw — and funded.

"I submitted three grants in the month after this course ended. Elena's framework for evaluating funder fit alone saved me weeks of wasted writing. This is the class I wish I'd had five years into my development career."

Maria T. — Development Coordinator, Chicago Food Pantry Network
Your instructor

Elena Park

Former Foundation Program Officer · Grant Writing Consultant

Elena spent eight years as a program officer at a regional community foundation, where she reviewed more than four hundred grant applications. She knows, from the other side of the table, what makes a proposal work — and what causes a reviewer to set it aside. Since 2018, she's consulted with small and mid-sized nonprofits across the country, helping organizations raise their first six-figure grant and retool their development programs for long-term sustainability.
